{"narrative":"You cup a hand around the flame and lean towards the harbourmaster’s desk. Salt has whitened the edges of the ledger beneath his elbow.

“The missing ship,” you say. “Has there been word?”

He lifts his head, studying you over spectacles repaired with twine. Then he draws a folded notice from beneath his mug.

“Word arrived this evening. She put into the next harbour with a split yard. Everyone aboard is safe.” He turns the notice so you can read it. “The pilot brought this himself.”

You lower the lantern. Beneath the account of damaged rigging, the captain has written the names of those aboard. Your finger travels down the list, leaving a pale streak through the dust on the desk. **No one is missing.**

“And the departure?” you ask.

“Cancelled. No sense sending a search boat after a ship already tied up.” The harbourmaster scratches a line through an entry in his ledger, shakes sand over the wet ink, and closes the book. “You can stay ashore tonight, mason.”

Through the open door, the sheltered water carries the wavering reflections of quay lamps. Somewhere close by, a loose halyard taps against a mast. *Such a small, ordinary sound.* You find yourself listening until your grip on the lantern loosens.

The harbourmaster sets a kettle beside the little iron stove and nudges a stool towards you with his boot.

“There’s tea, if you’ve finished worrying.” His mouth softens. “Or you can take the notice outside and read every name again.
